$schema_note: Bank / omnibus-wallet compliance scenarios. An OMNIBUS wallet = one commingled custody wallet holding funds for many customers (exchange hot wallets are the canonical real-world example). Real labeled addresses are used for the wallets, seeds, and sanctioned contracts. Edges marked "scenario": true (or listed in synthetic_addresses) are CONSTRUCTED test flows, not assertions that this exact transfer happened on-chain. Purpose: exercise how the screener reports when a bank's commingled wallet is exposed to tainted funds.
bank_controls: Screen the omnibus wallet itself AND every counterparty on deposit, not just the wallet.
On a direct sanctions hit (score >= 90): escalate to the compliance officer, evaluate reject/freeze before crediting, file a SAR where warranted.
Pooled funds are not attributed to a customer: treat a tainted inflow as a whole-pool exposure until the specific depositor is identified.
Do not dismiss a designated source on amount (dust rule). Amount reduces, but never erases, designated-source exposure.
Document the known gaps (no internal-transfer tracing on free RPCs; no off-chain legs) in every report.
Re-screen on an ongoing basis, not only at onboarding.

cases.title: Direct inflow from an OFAC-designated address
cases.scenario: A bank-run omnibus custody wallet (real example: a major exchange hot wallet) receives a transfer one hop from an OFAC-sanctioned address.
cases.why_it_matters: A sanctioned inbound transfer creates sanctions exposure for the entire commingled pool, not just one customer. Strict-liability sanctions regimes do not care that it was 12.5 out of thousands of ETH.

expected.action: Escalate; consider rejecting/freezing the credit; screen and block the counterparty; preserve evidence.

cases.title: Two-hop taint from a Lazarus-linked exploiter
cases.scenario: Tainted funds from the Bybit exploiter pass through one intermediary before landing in a second omnibus wallet.
cases.why_it_matters: Layering (one extra hop) lowers but does not remove exposure. Hop distance is a risk gradient, not a pass/fail line.

expected.action: Enhanced monitoring; trace full path; document the intermediary.

cases.title: One tainted depositor hidden among clean flows
cases.scenario: An omnibus wallet receives 150 ETH of clean retail deposits and 0.5 ETH from a hack-linked address. The wallet cannot tell which customer is which.
cases.why_it_matters: This is the core omnibus problem: a tiny tainted deposit taints the pool, and normal tools cannot name the responsible customer. Amount-based dismissal is unsafe when the source is a designated or hack-linked address.

expected.action: Do not dismiss on amount; investigate inbound deposit records; potential pool-level restriction.

cases.title: Outbound transfer to a sanctioned mixer
cases.scenario: An omnibus wallet sends funds directly to the OFAC-sanctioned Tornado Cash router.
cases.why_it_matters: Outbound exposure matters as much as inbound: sending to a sanctioned address is itself a prohibited dealing and a money-laundering red flag.

expected.action: Escalate; stop/recall if possible; file SAR; freeze relationship pending review.

cases.title: Commingling without taint: the custody-risk blind spot
cases.scenario: An omnibus wallet shows no path to any tainted seed, yet the operator can still commingle customer and corporate funds and become insolvent (real-world illustration: FTX). Taint screening cannot see this risk.
cases.why_it_matters: Screening answers 'is this money dirty?'. It does NOT answer 'is this custodian solvent / honest?'. Omnibus custody adds counterparty and commingling risk that taint scoring is blind to. A complete bank control set needs both.

expected.action: No taint action; rely on separate custody/counterparty due-diligence controls.

cases.title: Negative control: clean omnibus wallet
cases.scenario: A labeled exchange wallet receives only clean inflows and has no path to any seed within the hop cap. Must NOT flag.
cases.why_it_matters: False positives make an omnibus wallet unusable and cause de-risking that harms legitimate customers. The control asserts a clean wallet stays LOW.
